title: Self-awareness
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Keep it personal and kind: a child who is sad or angry at home is not asked to share in front of the class. Psalm 139:13-14 and Genesis 1:27 on the board all week.

skills.key_step: The child says that God made him or her on purpose (Psalm 139:13-14), in God's image (Genesis 1:27), and that every other child is special in the same way.

floor.prerequisite: Knows God made Adam and Eve.
floor.question: Who made the first man and woman?

representations: a hand-print wall where no two prints are the same
a picture of a potter shaping a pot
steps: Ask who knit the child together.
Read Genesis 1:27: made in God's image.
Say: special does not mean better than others.
contexts: twins in the class who are still different
a newborn baby in a family

board.do: Point at the hand-prints on the wall.
board.say: Are any two the same? Who made each of us?

board.do: Wait for the child to say God made each one.
Write: God made me, and God made you.

listen_for: You are better than other children
misconceptions.ask: What does it mean that you are God's special creation?
misconceptions.repair: Say that every child is special in the same way, and ask each child to name one thing that makes a classmate special.

misconceptions.ask: According to Psalm 139:13-14, how did God make you?
misconceptions.repair: Read Psalm 139:13-14 slowly and ask who is doing the knitting.

listen_for: God made only the first man and woman, and I came from my parents only
misconceptions.ask: Who made you, according to the Bible?
misconceptions.repair: Link Genesis 1:27 ("God created mankind in his own image") to Psalm 139:13 about each person.

listen_for: People have the same face as God
misconceptions.ask: What does it mean that people are made in the image of God (Genesis 1:27)?
misconceptions.repair: Show a photo and then a kind act: we show God's image by how we love, not by our faces. Every skin colour carries God's image.

checks.question: Who made you, according to Psalm 139:13?
Does being God's special creation make you better than other children?
checks.answer: No: God made every child special

skills.key_step: The child names good thoughts and feelings, says that anger is not itself a sin but must not lead to sin or be kept overnight (Ephesians 4:26), and that Christians rejoice in the Lord always (Philippians 4:4).

floor.prerequisite: Can say how he or she feels when happy or sad.
floor.question: Name one feeling you have when you are given a gift.

representations: faces showing happy, sad, angry and calm
Ephesians 4:26 and Philippians 4:4 on flash cards
a sun going down drawn on the board
steps: Read Ephesians 4:26: anger is not a sin, but do not sin in anger.
Read Philippians 4:4: rejoice in the Lord always, not only on good days.
contexts: a lost game in a football match
a sad day when a pet dies

board.do: Write "In your anger do not sin" (Ephesians 4:26) and draw a setting sun.

board.say: What should you do with anger before the sun goes down?

board.do: Wait for the child to say make peace, settle it.
Write: feel it, do not sin, settle it today.

misconceptions.ask: What does Ephesians 4:26 say about anger?
misconceptions.repair: Read the verse: it says "in your anger do not sin". Ask what the angry child can do instead of hitting or shouting.

listen_for: Keep it and pay the person back later
misconceptions.ask: What should you do about anger, according to Ephesians 4:26?
misconceptions.repair: Role-play saying sorry or forgiving before bedtime.

listen_for: Rejoice only when things go well
misconceptions.ask: What does Philippians 4:4 tell us to do?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether we can be thankful to God even on a hard day, and why.

misconceptions.ask: What does "do not let the sun go down while you are still angry" (Ephesians 4:26) teach?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: what happens at sunset? The day ends. So the verse says end your anger before the day ends.

checks.question: Is it a sin to feel angry, according to Ephesians 4:26?
checks.answer: No, but we must not sin when angry

checks.question: When does Philippians 4:4 say we should rejoice in the Lord?

skills.key_step: The child lists choices a child makes each day, gives the result of each, and chooses by asking what pleases God, even when friends choose differently.

floor.prerequisite: Can say what Adam and Eve chose and what followed.
floor.question: What happened after Adam and Eve disobeyed God?
floor.answer: They were sent out of the garden (they hid, they suffered)

representations: a choice and its result as two linked boxes
steps: List choices a child makes in one day.
Choose the right path even if friends choose another.
contexts: finding money on the school path
choosing a friend at break time

board.do: Draw a road that splits into two paths.
Point at the place where the road splits.
board.say: Your friends go left to skip class. Which path pleases God?

board.do: Wait for the child to choose and give a reason.
Write the result at the end of each path.

listen_for: There is no result because nobody saw
misconceptions.ask: Kamau takes a pencil that is not his and nobody sees. What is true?
misconceptions.repair: List the results of one choice: for the child, for the owner, and before God.

misconceptions.ask: Your friends tell you to skip class. How do you choose what to do?
misconceptions.repair: Role-play a polite NO and walking to class.

listen_for: Only deciding which school to attend
misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a choice a child makes?
misconceptions.repair: Make a list of the choices in one school morning.

misconceptions.ask: Achieng did not study and failed her test. Why did she fail?
misconceptions.repair: Draw two arrows from one choice to its result. Ask the child to finish three such pairs.

checks.question: Kamau takes a pencil that is not his and nobody sees. Is there a result?
checks.answer: Yes: he did wrong and he knows it

checks.question: How should you choose when friends choose wrong?
